answer: Any fable about cheap identities ends the same way: bind one identity to one physical device. Registration requires a TPM attestation quote proving the key was born inside real hardware and cannot be exported; a registry of device fingerprints guarantees one machine mints only one key. An attacker wanting a hundred sockpuppets must buy a hundred devices, paying retail each time — the nectar of free money dries up while an honest user pays once for the device they already own. At the zenith sits cross-checking: duplicate hardware quotes slash both identities and burn their stake.
